source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Harvest readiness is judged by looking at the two tendrils near the fruit stem: when about 70% of the tendril, from tip toward the base, has dried/withered, the fruit is ready. The fruit's rind should also feel noticeably thicker/harder. Harvest is done using a knife or pruning shears to cut the stem, then fruit is carefully transported and placed in a storage/collection area.

Harvest timing by variety maturity group: light/early-maturing varieties have a lifespan of about 55-60 days; medium-maturing varieties about 65-75 days; and late/heavy-maturing varieties about 80-90 days after planting.

Average yield is cited as about 15-17 tons per hectare.
